 Judgment

The appeal filed by the insurance company challenging the judgment and award dated 29.05.2014,
passed by the Fast Track Court-II and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Belagavi, in MVC No.1092/2013, contending that quantum of compensation is excessive one.

sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the respondents.
3. The occurrence of accident, injuries sustained by the claimant, coverage of insurance are not in dispute.

5. In the present case the claimant has suffered injury of right tibia.
The doctor has stated that the claimant has suffered 25% of physical disability towards right lover limb.

The tribunal has held 20%
as functional disability which is excessive one.
The claimant has suffered single fracture tibia of right leg.
Therefore, the tribunal is not correct in holding 20% as functional disability towards whole body.
Therefore, it is modified by applying principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar and another1.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar and another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, 10% as functional disability is taken into consideration.

Therefore, the compensation under loss of future income due to disability is modified as follows:
6.
The accident is caused in the year 2011.
Therefore, notional income of Rs.6,000/- per month is taken into consideration, which is recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
The claimant was (2011) 1 SCC 343 NC: 2023:KHC-D:13272 aged 45 years at the time of accident.
Therefore appropriate applicable multiplier is 14.

Hence, loss of future income due to disability is hereby reassessed and quantified as Rs.1,00,800/- (Rs.6,000 x 10% x 12 x 14).
7.
Further compensation awarded by the tribunal under various heads are kept intact.

Thus, the claimant is entitled for total compensation under various heads as under:
 Sl. Heads.

Amount in  No. (Rs.)
 1. Towards pain and suffering.

50,000  2. Towards loss of future happiness 50,400  and amenities.
 3. Towards loss of income during 24,000  the treatment period.
 4. Towards incidental charges.
24,000  5. Towards loss of future income.

Therefore, the claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,49,200/- as against what has been awarded by the tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal filed by the insurance company is allowed.
ii) The judgment and award dated 29.05.2014, passed by the Fast Track Court-II and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Belagavi, in MVC No.1092/2013, stands The Divisional Manager vs Manjunath Maruti More on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58892603/
3 modified to the aforesaid extent.
iii) The claimant is entitled total compensation of Rs.2,49,200/- along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
